atoms.b:
Rosa Parks (1913-2005)
Rosa Parks was born “Rosa Louise McCauley” on February 4, 1913, in Tuskegee, Alabama. Growing up in the South, she faced ((racial_discrimination)) daily and attended ((segregated)) schools. She could not finish college because her grandmother became ill.

At age 19, she married Raymond Parks, and together they worked in ((social_justice)) groups. Rosa became a key figure in the Civil Rights Movement, especially during the 1955 ((Montgomery_Bus_Boycott)). 75% of bus passengers in Montgomery were Black, but they had to sit at the back. Rosa Parks ((refused)) to give up her seat to a white passenger, which led to her arrest and loss of her job. The movement resulted in a bus boycott, a 13-month mass protest organised by Martin Luther King Jr. and led to the desegregation of public buses.

The Bus Boycott was an example of non-violent ((resistance))—that is, the use of peaceful tactics to challenge injustice. Around 1980, Rosa ((struggled)) with financial and health problems, after consistently giving financial and physical contributions to the movement. She died on October 24, 2005, in Detroit, Michigan, and lays in honor in the Capitol Rotunda.

instruction.text: Read the excerpt from an article about “Rosa Parks’ impact today”. Then, select the correct answer based on the article.

atoms.text: Especially for Black women, Rosa Parks’ impact is still very clear today. Her example helped bring Black women’s voices and leadership to the center of discussions about equal rights and justice. The movement is no longer only dominated by men. Because of the Civil Rights Movement, many more Black women are taking on leadership roles. They serve in public office and in courts, organizations and businesses.

atoms.a: Rosa Park's legacy is especially important for...
A remarkable change for Black women is...
b: a lack of rights and justice.
